<<set $day_step to 1>> The crack in the ceiling looks like a river delta. I've been staring at it long enough to name the tributaries. The main fissure runs diagonally from somewhere above the kitchenette to a point directly over my pillow a slow-motion fault line in cheap plaster that's been widening since I moved in eight months ago. There are smaller branches splitting off from it, hairline fractures that spider outward like the whole ceiling is a windshield that took a rock on the highway. Sometimes, in that grey zone between sleep and waking, I imagine I can hear it growing. A tiny, geological creak. The building settling further into its own decay. My phone alarm is going off. <img src="images/scenes/day_1/day_1_3.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> It's been going off for a while, actually. The sound has woven itself into whatever half-dream I was having something about being in a lobby that kept loading, a progress bar stuck at 99%, and a chat window scrolling too fast to read. The alarm is a default tone I never bothered to change, a cheerful marimba loop that feels like mockery at I fumble the phone off the floor beside the mattress and squint at the screen 11:47 AM. I set it for 10:30. The screen brightness stabs my eyes and I drop the phone face-down on my chest, blinking at the ceiling crack while my pupils adjust. My mouth tastes like the inside of a USB port. There's a dull ache behind my left eye that might be dehydration or might be the Monster Energy I drank at 3 AM finally metabolizing into regret. Both, probably. A Discord notification sits under the alarm. From last night. I already read it before I fell asleep read it twice, actually, like an idiot but my eyes find it again before I can stop them. <<kira "night eli! don't stay up too late okay? you need your beauty sleep 😴✨">> Beauty sleep. She said beauty sleep. With a sparkle emoji. I know it's a joke. I know she says stuff like that to everyone. Kira's the kind of person who calls people "babe" and "hon" the way other people say "dude" it doesn't mean anything, it's just her frequency, her warmth spilling out in all directions without a specific target. I know this. I've had this conversation with myself approximately four hundred times. I still read the message a third time before I put the phone down. I should get up. The mattress a queen-size I found on the sidewalk three blocks over, dragged home at midnight with Marcus's help, and swore I'd buy a frame for is on the floor against the wall beneath the window. The sheets are grey. They were white when I bought them from the dollar store but they've been through enough wash cycles in the basement machines to achieve a permanent, institutional grey that no amount of detergent will fix. The fitted sheet has popped off the far corner again and bunched up, exposing a yellowed stain on the mattress that was there when I found it and which I've chosen to believe is coffee. My apartment is a studio. That word studio does a lot of heavy lifting. It implies intention, like someone designed this 280-square-foot rectangle to be a living space rather than a storage unit that someone illegally subdivided and rented to a desperate 22-year-old for $875 a month. The kitchenette is against the far wall: a mini-fridge that hums at a frequency I can feel in my teeth, a hot plate, a microwave with a broken turntable so you have to open it and rotate your food manually halfway through. The bathroom is behind a door that doesn't fully close because the humidity warped the frame. There's a closet, but the rod fell down four months ago and I just pile clothes on the floor in there now and then there's the desk. The desk is the point of this whole arrangement. Everything else the mattress, the kitchenette, the oxygen exists in service to the desk. It's a battered wooden thing I pulled off the curb on bulk trash day, slightly warped on one side so my mouse pad slopes if I don't wedge a folded piece of cardboard under the left leg. On it: two monitors. The main one is a 24-inch I got refurbished for eighty bucks decent color, responsive enough for gaming, a scratch across the lower left corner that I've trained my eyes to ignore. The second is a 19-inch piece of shit with a cluster of dead pixels in the upper right that looks like a tiny permanent bruise on reality. I use it for chat and stream management. Between them, a budget USB microphone on a short desk stand that I have to lean toward when I talk, which means I spend entire streams slightly hunched, which is doing great things for my posture. The webcam is clipped to the top of the main monitor. It's old enough to be in a museum. In low light which is always, because my apartment has the ambient brightness of a crypt it makes my face look like it was rendered on a PlayStation 2. <img src="images/locations/eli_desk.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> No ring light. No acoustic panels. No branded overlay. No custom emotes. No sub badges. No alerts. Just a desk, two screens, a mic, a camera from the Obama administration, and the stubborn, stupid refusal to quit that I keep mistaking for ambition. I've seen Kira's setup in the background of her selfies. Pink-and-black custom keyboard. Dual monitors with clean bezels. Acoustic foam covered in anime posters. A ring light that makes her skin glow like she's being rendered in real time. Everything deliberate, everything polished, everything her and she built it from scratch, same as me, except hers actually worked. I pull myself upright. The sheets fall away. I'm wearing the same boxers and grey t-shirt I fell asleep in. My feet find the cold floor actual hardwood, the one accidental luxury of this apartment, except it's January and there's a draft from somewhere and the wood feels like it's been stored in a morgue. I shuffle to the bathroom. Don't look in the mirror. I've gotten good at this navigating the sink, the toilet, the shower, all without making eye contact with the glass. It's not that I'm horrified by what I see. It's worse than that. It's that what I see is nothing. Forgettable. A face that exists in the space between faces, the kind you'd scroll past in a lineup without your brain even registering it as a person. Sometimes I catch myself in a reflection a shop window, a dark phone screen and there's this half-second where I genuinely don't recognize myself. Not in a dramatic, dissociative way. Just in the way you don't notice a beige wall. <img src="images/locations/eli_bathroom.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> Kira posted a selfie in the Discord last week. New earrings little dangling stars, silver, catching the light from her ring light. She had that look she does, the half-smirk with one eyebrow slightly raised, like she knows something you don't and might tell you if you ask nicely. Her bob was freshly cut, the bangs sitting perfectly straight across her forehead. She captioned it "new earrings who dis" and I spent eleven minutes trying to come up with a reply that was funny without being weird, flirty without being desperate, casual without being indifferent. I settled on a thumbs up emoji. A thumbs up. Like a forty-year-old dad reacting to a family group chat. She hearted it, which either meant she found it endearing or she was being polite to a sad person, and I'll never know which. Shower. Lukewarm because the hot water takes eight minutes to arrive and I'm not waiting. I wash my hair with the same bar soap I use on my body because shampoo is a luxury I keep forgetting to prioritize. The water pressure is a joke a thin, dispirited stream that couldn't rinse a thought, let alone the grease out of my hair. I get out, towel off with the one towel I own formerly navy, now a streaky grey-blue that matches the sheets in their shared journey toward entropy. Clothes. The rotation is three t-shirts: black (least stained), grey (softest), dark green with some graphic that's cracked and peeled beyond recognition (most comfortable). Today is a black t-shirt day. Same joggers as yesterday. Same joggers as the day before. They're black, which means they hide everything, which means they're clean until proven otherwise. I catch myself, for one stupid second, wondering what Kira would think of this outfit. Then I remember that "outfit" implies a decision was made, and what I'm wearing is less a choice than a default state, and that Kira who shows up to casual hangouts in band tees and platform sneakers like she just stepped off the set of a music video about being effortlessly cool would probably not have a thought about my joggers one way or the other. Stop thinking about her. Stream first. Self-loathing later. <img src="images/locations/eli_kitchen.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> Breakfast is an act of optimism performed with the materials of despair. I open the mini-fridge: half a bottle of generic-brand yellow mustard, a sleeve of American cheese slices with the edges curling, two Monster Energy cans, and something in a Tupperware container that I can't identify and don't open. The freezer has a stack of microwave burritos. I take one, nuke it for two minutes (opening the microwave at one minute to manually rotate it because the turntable's broken, like I said), and eat it standing at the counter while it's still molten in the center and frozen at one end. This is fine. This is fuel. I wash it down with a Monster the green one, original flavor, the only consistent thing in my life. 11:58 AM. I pull it in. The desk wobbles. I adjust the cardboard wedge under the left leg with my foot. Open the main monitor: wallpaper is the default Windows 11 bloom that I never changed. Desktop cluttered with game shortcuts, unsorted screenshots, and a folder called "Stream Assets" that contains exactly two files a PNG of my stream name in a free font and a JPEG of a "be right back" screen I made in Paint. Gunmetal Requiem competitive tactical shooter, biggest game on Twitch right now. I'm not good at it. I'm not bad enough to be funny and not good enough to be impressive. The thing about streaming to no one is that you can hear your own voice bouncing off the walls of the room, and after a while you start to realize that you're essentially talking to yourself in a room you're paying rent on, into a microphone nobody's listening to, while a camera nobody's watching records your face for no one to see. That hasn't happened in months. Maybe longer. [[Take of the wig and Leave Facility|day_3_23_kira]]<<set $hint to "Leave the clinic">> <<set $playerImage = "images/user/tier_0_2.jpeg">> <<set $day_step to 23>> I leave the clinic with a bag containing the wig and the care kit and the receipt for the brow sculpt 300 $, seven-day payment window and I walk four blocks back to my apartment in the January cold with my new lashes catching snowflakes I didn't notice starting and my new brows still subtly reshaping beneath the skin and the wig in a bag that swings from my hand like a prop from a life I'm rehearsing for. The splinter in my chest is there. I can feel it small, sharp, positioned in the exact place where the warm pulse of Kira's red heart lives. Two sensations occupying the same space: the guilt and the hope, the lie and the love, the secret and the girl who doesn't know it exists. I check my phone. Two hours until Kira picks me up. Two hours to hide everything. <<link "Go Home">><<set $hint to "Go Home and Wait in Bedroom">><<goto neighbourhood>><</link>>I spend the two hours before Kira arrives in a state of controlled panic. The wig is in the closet, buried beneath the pile of clothes on the floor where the rod fell four months ago. The care kit is shoved behind the mini-fridge. The RegenaForm receipt is deleted from my email and the browser history is cleared and the confirmation page is closed and every digital trace of the afternoon has been scrubbed with the thoroughness of a person who watches too many crime procedurals and not enough relationship advice videos. The physical traces are harder to hide. I stand in the bathroom. I look in the mirror. Not the phone camera the actual mirror, the one I've been avoiding for eight months, the one that shows everything without filter or mercy. The eyelashes are there. Long, dark, dense. They catch the light from the flickering overhead bulb and cast tiny shadows on my cheekbones that weren't there yesterday. The brows are reshaping I can see it happening in real time, the slow migration from thick-masculine to feathered-feminine, the arch lifting by degrees, the hair refining itself from scraggly to sculpted. Dr. Maren said two to three hours. It's been ninety minutes. The transformation is halfway done. Will she notice? Of course she'll notice. Kira notices everything. She noticed the shampoo. She noticed when I changed my stream title two months ago. She noticed the brand of energy drink I switched to in September and asked if I was okay because "people only change energy drinks when something's wrong." She is an observation engine disguised as a girl with wire-frame glasses and she will look at my face and she will see the lashes and the brows and she will ask and I will lie. The plan "new skincare routine" feels paper-thin, a tissue-paper excuse stretched over a truth-shaped hole. But it's what I have and it might work, because the changes are subtle, because the lashes look natural, because the brows are only halfway to their final shape, because Kira has never paid close attention to my brow line (probably I don't actually know what Kira has and hasn't paid attention to, given that she apparently memorized my 3 AM voice and my thumbnail-picking habit from video calls). I splash water on my face. Pat dry. Look in the mirror one more time. The face looking back is mine. Different, but mine. The lashes make my eyes look bigger. The partially reshaped brows make my forehead look smoother. The combined effect is what did Dr. Maren say? lighter. The face is lighter. More open. Not feminine, not yet, but softer in a way that's hard to pin down, like someone adjusted the contrast settings on a photograph. My phone buzzes. <<kira "leaving in 10! i'm bringing snacks. you better have cleared a space on that couch">> <<eli "i don't have a couch">> <<kira "your mattress. you better have cleared a space on your mattress. actually no we're watching at my place. your apartment makes me sad">> <<eli "it makes me sad too">> <<kira "then it's settled. my place. Packet misses you">> <<eli "i met Packet once and he hissed at me">> <<kira "that's his love language 😤">> I smile. The muscles ache less today. They're adapting. [[Kira picks arrive|day_3_25_kira]]<<set $hint to "Go with Kira">> <<set $locationImage to "images/locations/neighbourhood.jpeg">> <<set $locationName to "Street">> She picks me up at 6:07. Seven minutes late because she stopped to buy mochi from her mom's bakery ("Mom asked who I was bringing snacks for and I said 'a friend' and she gave me the look, Eli. THE LOOK. The Japanese-mother-who-knows-everything look."). I get in the Civic. Cherry blossom. Heater. The warm, enclosed space that smells like her. She's wearing a cream cardigan over a black tank top, her hair freshly washed and slightly fluffier than usual, the bob bouncing at her jawline. The wire-frame glasses are slightly crooked she pushes them up as I close the door. <<kira "Hi.">> <<eli "Hi.">> She leans across the console. I lean to meet her. The kiss is quick a hello kiss, a punctuation mark, a "this is a thing we do now" kiss and her lips are warm and taste like the mochi she was sampling in the car. When she pulls back, she looks at my face. She looks at my face for three seconds. My heart rate spikes. Not the warm spike from yesterday's kiss the cold spike, the adrenaline spike, the "she's going to see it" spike that sends electricity through my fingertips and makes my mouth go dry. <<kira "Did you do something to your face?">> There it is. The question. The one I prepared for, rehearsed, armed myself against. She asks it lightly not accusatory, not suspicious, just curious, the tone of someone who notices a change in a face they've been studying for eighteen months. <<eli "New skincare routine.">> The lie exits my mouth with a smoothness that surprises me. Three words, evenly delivered, the vocal equivalent of a shrug. I even add a self-deprecating half-smile, the kind that says "I know, I know, I'm finally taking care of myself, don't make it a thing." Kira squints. Her eyes narrow behind the glasses not suspicion, not yet, but the focused attention of a person whose brain just flagged something without quite identifying it. She's looking at my lashes. I can feel her gaze on them, two points of heat on my eyelids. <<kira "Hmm.">> One syllable. Noncommittal. She doesn't push. Kira has this gift the same gift Marcus has of letting people keep their mysteries, of filing observations without demanding explanations. She heard my answer. She weighed it. She found it insufficient and she chose to let it go. For now. <<kira "Well, it's working. You look good.">> <<eli "Thanks.">> <<kira "Like, actually good. Your eyes look... different. Brighter.">> <<eli "It's the skincare routine.">> <<kira "What products? I might need to try them.">> <<eli "Uh. I don't remember the brand. It was at the drugstore.">> <<kira "You bought skincare products at a drugstore and you don't remember the brand?">> <<eli "I'm a guy, Kira. We just grab things.">> She looks at me for one more second. Then she puts the car in drive and pulls away from the curb and the moment passes, and the splinter in my chest pushes a fraction of a millimeter deeper and I think: that was close. That was the first test. There will be more. [[Arrive at Kira's apartment|day_3_26_kira]]<<set $hint to "Spend time with Kira">> <<set $locationImage to "images/locations/kira_apartment.jpeg">> <<set $locationName to "Kira's Apartment">> Kira's apartment is warm and lit and alive in the way my apartment is cold and dim and dying. Packet the grey tabby, the keyboard sitter, the hisser is on the couch when we walk in. He looks at me with the flat, appraising gaze of an animal that knows things humans don't, and I swear he can see through the eyelashes and the brows and the lie to the person underneath. <<kira "Packet, be nice. Eli's our guest.">> Packet does not be nice. Packet stares at me for four seconds, then turns his back and begins washing his paw with the elaborate disinterest of a creature that considers me beneath its notice. I respect this. Packet and I have an understanding: I don't expect affection and he doesn't provide any. It's the most honest relationship in this apartment. <<kira "Tea?">> <<eli "Sure.">> She disappears into the kitchen. I hear the kettle fill, the burner click. I stand in the living room the grey sectional, the coffee table with the manga and the orchid figurine now moved to a small shelf, the framed prints on the walls. Kira's apartment is curated the way her stream is curated every object chosen, every placement intentional, the physical space reflecting the same aesthetic control she applies to her digital one. It's not obsessive. It's just... considered. The apartment of a person who thinks about where things go and why. My apartment is the apartment of a person who dropped things and left them where they fell. She returns with two mugs. Tea green, the good kind, not the bag-in-a-cup kind. She hands me one and settles onto the couch, drawing her legs up beneath her, and pats the cushion beside her. <<kira "Sit. I queued up an anime. The couch cushions are firm and supportive everything in Kira's life is firm and supportive, including the couch and the career and the girl herself and I sink into them the way I sink into her company. Packet, having completed his paw-washing, relocates to the arm of the couch with the resigned tolerance of a cat who's accepted that the couch is no longer exclusively his territory. Kira starts the show. The screen glows. The opening credits play soft music, painted backgrounds, the kind of animation that looks like watercolors in motion. She tucks herself against my side with the natural, practiced motion of someone who's been waiting to do this, and I lift my arm and it goes around her shoulders and her head finds the hollow between my shoulder and my chest and she fits there like the space was designed for her. Her hair is against my jaw. I can smell her shampoo something floral, different from the cherry blossom of the car, more personal, the scent of her actual head on my actual shoulder. Her glasses press into my collarbone. She adjusts them without looking, one hand reaching up to tilt the frames so they're not digging in, and her fingers brush my neck in the process and the touch sends a ripple down my spine that I absorb without moving. <<kira "Comfortable?">> <<eli "Yeah.">> <<kira "Good. No moving for the next three episodes.">> <<eli "Three?">> <<kira "Minimum. Frieren requires commitment.">> We watch. The anime is she's right, it's beautiful. A story about time and loss and the slow realization that the things you didn't pay attention to were the things that mattered most. An immortal elf looking back at a life she lived alongside mortals and understanding, too late, that the moments she dismissed as trivial were the only ones worth keeping. I watch it and I feel things. Not the numb, flat nothing that usually occupies the space behind my sternum during screen time, but actual, genuine things sadness and warmth and the ache of recognition, the specific ache of watching a character realize they wasted time and knowing you're doing the same thing. Kira shifts against me, adjusting her position, pressing closer. I hold her tighter. Not dramatically just a fractional increase in the arm around her shoulders, a thumb moving slowly against the fabric of her cardigan. She makes a sound. A small "mmm" of contentment, barely audible, more vibration than voice. The second episode ends. The third starts. Kira's commentary which was frequent and passionate during the first episode ("LOOK at that background, Eli, LOOK at it") has gotten quieter. Her voice is softer. Her observations are shorter. The gaps between them are longer. Halfway through the third episode, she stops talking entirely. I look down. Her eyes are closed. Her breathing has changed slower, deeper, the rhythm of sleep. Her glasses have slipped down her nose. One hand is resting on my chest, the fingers loosely curled, the pixel-heart tattoo visible on her inner wrist. Her lips are slightly parted. There's a strand of hair across her cheek that the breathing moves, gently, back and forth, back and forth. She's asleep. Kira Nomura 12,400 followers, 890 average viewers, $487 per session, bisexual, sharp-tongued, wire-framed, the most competent person I've ever met is asleep on my shoulder at 8:45 PM on a Thursday in January, and I am going to sit here without moving for as long as she sleeps because waking her would be a crime. I sit perfectly still. I breathe shallowly. The anime plays the third episode continues, and I watch it over the top of her head, and the story unfolds, and the elf mage learns something about humans that she should have known before, and Kira sleeps against me with the trusting weight of a person who feels safe. Packet, who has been observing from the arm of the couch, stands, stretches, and walks across the cushions to settle on Kira's lap. He curls into a circle, tucks his nose into his tail, and begins to purr. The vibration transfers through Kira's body into mine. Two living things, warm and sleeping and touching, and me awake, holding them both, the stillest I've been in months. I think about the eyelashes. The brows. The wig in my closet. The ElliePlayz dashboard with its $47 and its 51 followers. The RegenaForm receipt I deleted from my email. The lie I told thirty minutes ago in this car "new skincare routine" and the way Kira squinted and said "hmm" and let it go. The splinter. I can feel it now, deeper than before, positioned between the warmth of her body and the cold calculation of my afternoon. Two realities coexisting in the same chest: the real and the secret. The girl who fell asleep trusting me and the person I'm becoming without telling her. She's on my shoulder and I have her trust and I'm going to go home tonight and put on a wig and sit in front of a webcam and pretend to be a woman for money. The anime ends. A fourth episode auto-plays. Kira sleeps through it. Packet purrs. I don't move. I sit there for forty minutes. [[Wait till Kira wakes up|day_3_27_kira]]<<set $day_step to 27>> She wakes at 9:30. Then she pulls back and steps inside and the door closes and I stand in the hallway with her fingerprints on my face and her trust in my pocket and the lie between my teeth like a seed I can't swallow and can't spit out. <<set $hint to "Go Home and Stream">> [[Go Home|apartment_map]]I get home at 10:15. The apartment. The crack. The hum. I close the door. Stand in the dark. Don't turn on the light. The January night presses against the window and the building settles and the pipes clank and I stand there in my grey shirt with the drool spot on the shoulder and I feel the two realities pressing against each other inside my chest like tectonic plates. The warm one: Kira. The couch. The sleeping. The trust. The kiss. The cold one: ElliePlayz. The dashboard. The $47. The 89 viewers. The clinic. The wig in the closet. Both real. Both mine. Frame the shot from the nose up without nose visibility. eyes, eyelashes, eye brows,forehead and the cascade of wig-hair falling from the top of my head. I angle my desk lamp to the side, creating a warm, directional light that softens the jaw shadow and makes the skin look smoother than it is. In the preview, from the nose up without nose visibility, in this lighting, with this wig, I look like I look like a girl. Not a beautiful girl. Not a convincing girl. But a plausible one. A girl who's shy about showing her face. A girl who streams with the camera low because she's nervous. I hover over "Go Live." The key works. $210 today. From half a face. From eyes and lashes and brows and hair from the nose up, from the feminized slice, from the fraction I'm willing to show. Half a face earned $210. Not even half a face, really. A quarter of a face, if you think about it. The eyes and hair, the part that reads feminine, the part that performs. The part that makes people say "those eyes could END me." The part that makes people click and stay and donate and simper and build a community around a person who doesn't exist. height:auto;"> I lie on my back, staring at the ceiling. No phone. No music. Just the low hum of the building and the faint sound of traffic somewhere outside. My body sinks into the mattress slowly, tension I didn't know I was holding easing out of my shoulders. <<eli "...just needed a minute.">> I don't sleep. Just exist for a while. It helps more than it should. [[← Bed|eli_bed]]<img src="images/locations/eli_bed.jpeg" alt="Eli's Bed" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> I roll onto my side and pull the blanket up without bothering to get under it properly. The room is dim, quiet. My eyes drift half-closed. Thoughts float in scattered, weightless, not really landing on anything. <<eli "...brain's just... going.">> A loose, directionless kind of rest. Not sleep, not awake. Something in between. [[← Bed|eli_bed]]<img src="images/locations/eli_bed.jpeg" alt="Eli's Bed" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> I sit up against the headboard, knees pulled up, and just... breathe. The apartment is still. The kind of quiet that feels thick, like it has weight. My chest is tight in a way I can't explain. I let it be tight. Don't push it. <<eli "...it'll pass.">> Eventually my shoulders drop. Eventually my jaw unclenches. It takes longer than it should. [[← Bed|eli_bed]]<img src="images/locations/eli_bed.jpeg" alt="Eli's Bed" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> Face down. Arms under the pillow. The mattress is warm from earlier and I sink into it without thinking. Everything muffles the sound, the light, the low-grade noise in my head. <<eli "...yeah.">> It's not even tiredness. Just the need to press myself against something solid for a while. [[← Bed|eli_bed]]<img src="images/locations/eli_bed.jpeg" alt="Eli's Bed" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> I lie on my back and let my mind wander. Think about nothing in particular a conversation from three days ago, the way the light looked this morning, something I can't quite place. The ceiling stays the same. <<eli "...I need to get out more.">> The thought surfaces and sinks again. I don't move. [[← Bed|eli_bed]]<img src="images/locations/eli_bed.jpeg" alt="Eli's Bed" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> I grab my phone, scroll for a few minutes, then set it down screen-first without really reading anything. The room is dim. I close my eyes just to rest them. The sounds of the building settle around me a pipe somewhere, a door two floors up. <<eli "...just five minutes.">> My breathing slows on its own. Five minutes turns into fifteen. [[← Bed|eli_bed]]<<set $rand to random(1, 5)>> <<if $rand is 1>> <<goto bed_dream_1>> <<elseif $rand is 2>> <<goto bed_dream_2>> <<elseif $rand is 3>> <<goto bed_dream_3>> <<elseif $rand is 4>> <<goto bed_dream_4>> <<else>> <<goto bed_nodream>> <</if>><img src="images/locations/eli_bed.jpeg" alt="Eli's Bed" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> I'm out fast. Deeper than usual. The dream is a hallway I've never been in. Long, low-lit, doors on both sides. I'm looking for something I don't know what and the floor keeps shifting slightly underfoot. Someone is walking ahead of me. I can't see their face but I know I know them. I keep calling out but no sound comes. They turn a corner. Gone. I wake up with that specific hollow feeling of something lost that never existed. <<eli "...what was that.">> The room is dark. I check the time. More time has passed than it felt like. [[← Bed|eli_bed]]<img src="images/locations/eli_bed.jpeg" alt="Eli's Bed" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> The dream is bright, which feels wrong. Outside somewhere a street, maybe, or a park. Everything is slightly too saturated, the sky an impossible flat blue. There's someone beside me. A girl. I can't quite look at her directly, the way you sometimes can't in dreams. But she's there. We're walking. It feels easy. Normal. I don't want it to end and that's probably what wakes me up. <<eli "...hm.">> I lie there for a moment, not moving, trying to hold onto the edges of it. They dissolve anyway. [[← Bed|eli_bed]]<img src="images/locations/eli_bed.jpeg" alt="Eli's Bed" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> The dream doesn't make sense even inside it. I'm in this apartment but it's bigger, the rooms keep adding. There's a stream playing somewhere my setup but not my setup. Chat is moving but I can't read any of it. The numbers keep climbing and then resetting. I'm trying to say something into the mic but I've forgotten what. I wake up mildly anxious and immediately annoyed about it. <<eli "...great. Even in my sleep.">> I pull the blanket up and stare at the ceiling until the feeling passes. [[← Bed|eli_bed]]<img src="images/locations/eli_bed.jpeg" alt="Eli's Bed" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> It starts familiar my old place, the one before this one. The layout's wrong but the feeling is right, that specific low-ceilinged quiet. Someone else is there, moving around in the other room. I don't go in. I just stand in the hallway listening to them exist. It doesn't feel sad until I wake up. <<eli "...okay.">> I sit on the edge of the bed for a moment. Let the dream finish settling. Then I get up. [[← Bed|eli_bed]]<img src="images/locations/eli_bed.jpeg" alt="Eli's Bed" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> I'm out the moment my head hits the pillow. No transition. No awareness of falling asleep. Just nothing the clean, flat dark of a dreamless sleep. I wake up disoriented, unsure for a second where I am. Then the room assembles itself. Ceiling. Walls. The same place. <<eli "...didn't even feel like time passed.">> Heavy and rested in equal measure. I lie there blinking until I feel real again. [[← Bed|eli_bed]]<<set $locationName to "Eli's Apartment - Closet">> <<set $right_sidebar_mode to 0>> <<set $locationImage to "images/locations/eli_closet.jpeg">> <img src="images/locations/eli_closet.jpeg" alt="Eli's Closet" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> [[Change Clothes|closet_change]] | [[← Floor Plan|apartment_map]]<<set $rand to random(1, 5)>> <<if $rand is 1>> <<goto closet_outfit_1>> <<elseif $rand is 2>> <<goto closet_outfit_2>> <<elseif $rand is 3>> <<goto closet_outfit_3>> <<elseif $rand is 4>> <<goto closet_outfit_4>> <<else>> <<goto closet_outfit_5>> <</if>><img src="images/locations/eli_closet.jpeg" alt="Eli's Closet" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> I pull out the grey hoodie. It's the one I always go back to slightly worn at the cuffs, a small bleach stain near the pocket that I stopped noticing a long time ago. Dark jeans. The same ones as yesterday, probably. <<eli "...this works.">> I pull it on. Nothing fits great. Nothing needs to. [[← Closet|eli_closet]]<img src="images/locations/eli_closet.jpeg" alt="Eli's Closet" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> There's one clean black t-shirt left. Slightly wrinkled from the drawer but not bad enough to care about. I pair it with sweatpants and call it done. <<eli "Clean enough.">> I check myself in the closet mirror for exactly one second. Fine. [[← Closet|eli_closet]]<img src="images/locations/eli_closet.jpeg" alt="Eli's Closet" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> The navy crewneck I almost never wear. I grab it anyway it's near the front, which means everything else is either dirty or buried. Worn jeans, the ones with the frayed left knee. <<eli "...this'll do.">> A little more put-together than usual. Barely. [[← Closet|eli_closet]]<img src="images/locations/eli_closet.jpeg" alt="Eli's Closet" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> Nothing looks clean. I sniff a shirt a plain white one, slightly creased. It passes. I pull it on over boxers and reach for the joggers crumpled on the closet floor. <<eli "It's fine, nobody's coming over.">> Good enough for staying in. [[← Closet|eli_closet]]<img src="images/locations/eli_closet.jpeg" alt="Eli's Closet" style="width:100%; height:auto;"> I dig toward the back and find the olive green jacket I forgot I owned. Throw it over a plain tee. It actually fits okay. Better than okay. I leave the jeans from this morning on they're still clean enough. <<eli "...not bad.">> I almost look like I have somewhere to be. The room smells like laundry detergent for once fresh, almost unfamiliar. <<marc "yo, welcome.">> <<eli "why does it smell… good in here?">> <<marc "did laundry. don’t make it a thing.">> I steps in, sniffing the air like I didn’t trust it. <<eli "this is weird.">> <<marc "you’re weird.">> Marc tosses a clean hoodie onto the chair. <<marc "you should try it sometime.">> <<eli "don’t start.">> We both sit. <<marc "you stream earlier?">> <<eli "yeah. same outcome.">> <<marc "consistent, at least.">> <<eli "consistently bad.">> Marc nudges him lightly. <<marc "consistency’s step one.">> <<eli "what’s step two?">> <<marc "not quitting.">> I says it like it’s simple. I stares at the floor. <<eli "yeah…">> I stands after a moment. <<eli "i’ll head out.">> <<marc "later, man.">> <<eli "later. good night.">> [[Leave|neighbourhood]]<<nobr>> <<set $right_sidebar_mode (State.variables.sc || 0) : 0; var scDisp = el('mer-sc-display'); if (scDisp) scDisp.textContent = scVal.toLocaleString() + ' $'; renderTiers(); // Close overlay on button var closeBtn = document.getElementById('mer-btn-close'); if (closeBtn) closeBtn.addEventListener('click', function() { el('mer-overlay').classList.add('mer-hidden'); }); // Close overlay on backdrop click var overlay = document.getElementById('mer-overlay'); if (overlay) overlay.addEventListener('click', function(e) { if (e.target === this) el('mer-overlay').classList.add('mer-hidden'); }); }); })(); <</script>><a href="https://www.patreon.com/c/ElliePlayz" target="_blank">Patreon</a><<set $firstTimeSplash to true>> <<set $locationImage to "images/locations/eli_apartment.jpeg">> <<set $day to 1>> <<set $day_step to 0>> <<set $playerImage to "images/user/tier_0/face.jpeg">> / --- RIGHT SIDEBAR MODE --- 0 = real life | 1 = stream Set this each passage to control what the right bar shows. / <<set $right_sidebar_mode to 0>> / --- REAL LIFE STATS --- / <<set $money to 47>> <<set $loan to 0>> <<set $appearance to 2>> <<set $femininity to 0>> <<set $confidence to 2>> /* <<set $sexuality to 5>> / 0 = straight 100 = gay / */ <<set $female_attractiveness to 100>> <<set $male_attractiveness to 0>> <<set $stress to 90>> <<set $corruption to 0>> <<set $phone_msgs to []>> / --- STREAM STATS --- / <<set $viewers to 0>> <<set $followers to 54>> <<set $donations to 0>> <<set $sc to 0>> / --- HINT --- / <<set $hint to "Go through Introduction.">><span style="color: red;">The year is 2027, and the machines took the jobs before anyone figured out what comes next.</span> It didn't happen the way the movies promised no chrome skeletons marching through cities, no single moment where the switch flipped and humanity became obsolete. It happened the way everything happens in capitalism, gradually, then all at once. A chatbot replaced the call center. An algorithm replaced the paralegal. A vision model replaced the radiologist, the quality inspector, the truck driver, the copywriter, the graphic designer, the junior accountant, the data entry clerk, the customer service rep, the translator, the tutor, the social media manager, the content moderator, the warehouse picker, the fast-food line cook. One by one, then ten by ten, then by the thousands positions dissolving like sugar in hot water, there one quarter and gone the next, replaced by subscriptions to software that didn't need bathroom breaks or health insurance or the will to live. <img src="images/scenes/day_1/day_1_4.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> By 2026, the unemployment numbers had stopped meaning anything because the government kept redefining "employed" to include gig work that paid less than the electricity it required. The official rate said 7%. The real number the one that counted people who'd stopped looking, people working four gig apps simultaneously to make rent, people whose "job" was selling plasma and filling out surveys for fractions of a cent was closer to 25%. A quarter of the working-age population, untethered, drifting through an economy that had automated their purpose and offered nothing in return except a login screen and a suggestion to "build your personal brand." <img src="images/scenes/day_1/day_1_6.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> The streaming economy exploded not because people wanted to be entertainers but because there was nothing else left. Twitch, YouTube, TikTok, a dozen platforms that rose and fell like empires in fast-forward together they absorbed the displaced millions the way a sponge absorbs a flood, messily, inadequately, with most of the water ending up on the floor. Every laid-off barista became a Just Chatting streamer. Every automated-out office worker became a gaming channel. Every college graduate who discovered that their $80,000 degree qualified them for exactly zero positions that still existed sat down in front of a webcam and said "hey guys, welcome to the stream" and hoped with the quiet, animal desperation of a species watching its habitat shrink that someone would watch. Someone rarely did. <img src="images/scenes/day_1/day_1_5.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> The streaming economy operates on the same distribution as a casino, a handful of jackpots subsidized by millions of empty pockets. The top 1% of streamers capture 90% of the revenue. The rest stream into the void, burning hours and electricity and hope, performing for audiences of bots and ghosts and one persistent troll who shows up every day to remind them they're failing. The barrier to entry is zero a laptop and a Wi-Fi connection which means the competition is infinite, which means the browse page is a graveyard of thumbnail faces scrolling past at terminal velocity, each one a person who bet their future on being interesting enough to stop the scroll. The algorithm decides who lives and who dies. Not literally not yet but in the economic sense that matters. The recommendation engine, the browse page, the For You feed, these are the gods of the new economy, and they are neither kind nor fair. They reward engagement. They reward retention. They reward, above all else, the specific neurological response that a human face triggers in a human brain the click, the pause, the stay and some faces trigger it more than others. <img src="images/scenes/day_1/day_1_7.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> The data is clear, uncomfortable, and universally understood by anyone who's spent a week trying to grow a channel, attractive women outperform everyone. Not because they're better at games or funnier or smarter some are, some aren't, the distribution is normal but because the audience that funds the streaming economy is predominantly male, and predominantly lonely (lonelier now, in the post-automation quiet, with fewer workplaces to meet people and fewer reasons to leave the apartment), and the algorithm has learned to feed that loneliness with faces it can't look away from. The gender gap in streaming isn't a whisper. It's a scream. A female streamer with 500 viewers will, on average, earn three to five times the donations of a male streamer with the same count. The thumbnail click-through rate for a female face is 200% higher. The subscription retention is double. Everyone knows this. Nobody says it out loud. The industry pretends the meritocracy is real be consistent, engage with chat, find your niche because the alternative is admitting that the single most important variable in a streaming career is the genetic lottery. You can't put that in a YouTube thumbnail. Or you couldn't. Until RegenaForm. [[RegenaForm|start_2]] | <<link "Skip Introduction">><<set $hint to "Find your Apartment and Bed">><<goto neighbourhood>><</link>>RegenaForm appeared two years ago, quietly, the way all dangerous things appear a website, a waiting list, a whisper network among streamers and influencers and the body-conscious edges of the internet. No Super Bowl ad. No billboard campaign. Just a chrome double-helix logo and a six-word tagline that embedded itself in the collective consciousness like a splinter, <<img "images/regenaform/regenaform_logo_main.svg">> The technology behind RegenaForm is proprietary, patented, and classified at a level that makes pharmaceutical companies look transparent. What's public is this, they use the client's own DNA as a template. Every modification every reshaped bone, every restructured tissue, every new configuration of flesh and nerve is grown from the client's genetic material, activated by a bioactive compound that switches on dormant developmental pathways in existing cells. The body doesn't reject the changes because the changes are the body. There's nothing foreign. Nothing synthetic. Nothing that a blood test or a biopsy would flag as artificial. <img src="images/locations/regenaform_street_entrance.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> The results are immediate. The recovery is hours, not weeks. There are no scars. No suture lines. No telltale marks of any kind not a stitch, not a seam, not a single visible trace that anything was done at all. A jawline can be reshaped in forty minutes. Cheekbones restructured over a lunch break. Skin cleared, smoothed, re-toned to any shade on the human spectrum in the time it takes to watch a movie. Eyelashes grow from the same follicles they always lived in just longer, darker, denser, as if the body finally remembered what it was supposed to look like all along and that's just the face. RegenaForm's catalog extends from the cosmetic to the radical, with nothing off the table and no procedure considered too extreme. Voices can be modulated organically not through software but through actual restructuring of the vocal cords, the larynx, the resonance chambers of the throat and sinuses, producing a voice so authentically different that a spectrograph can't tell it from one that was born, not built. Body contour shoulders narrowed, waists cinched, hips widened, ribcages tapered, fat redistributed along any line the client desires achieved through skeletal and soft tissue modification that leaves the skin unblemished, the body unmarked, as though the bones had always been this shape. Breasts can be grown. Not implanted grown. From the client's own mammary tissue, activated and expanded, producing breasts in any size from barely-there to physics-defying. Any shape, teardrop, round, perky, natural. Any sensitivity level, from standard to hyper-responsive, the nerve density calibrated like a dial. Fully functional. Full sensation. Indistinguishable from natal development by any examination mammogram, biopsy, ultrasound because they are natal development, triggered decades after the original window closed. Breasts can be removed. Completely. The same technology that activates growth can reverse it the tissue reabsorbs into the body, the mammary cells deactivate, the skin tightens and smooths until the chest is flat, contoured, masculine or androgynous or whatever the client specifies. No mastectomy scars. No asymmetry. No trace. A person could grow D-cups on a Monday and have a flat chest by Wednesday and no medical scan on Thursday would find evidence of either state. The body simply reorganizes itself around the new instruction, as indifferent to the direction of change as water is to the shape of its container. <img src="images/scenes/day_1/day_1_8.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> Buttocks reshaped grown fuller or reduced to nothing. Hips flared wide or narrowed to a masculine frame. Waists cinched to proportions that corsets couldn't achieve or thickened to a straight, angular torso. Every modification seamless, scarless, grown from within and removable from within. The body rebuilds itself around the new blueprint, and the new blueprint leaves no evidence of the old one. Nor does the reversal leave evidence of the blueprint before that. At the far end of the catalog, behind a consultation wall and a financial threshold that filters out everyone except the desperate and the committed, full genital construction. In any direction. A vulva built from the client's own cells labia, clitoris, vaginal canal self-lubricating, fully sensate, connected to a nervous system that was rewired to receive its signals as pleasure, as sensation, as the authentic experience of a body that matches its configuration. A uterus. Ovaries. Fallopian tubes. The complete architecture of a female reproductive system, grown inside a body that was born male, operating on hormones that the body now produces naturally because RegenaForm didn't just add parts it rewrote the endocrine system from the ground up. Full fertility optional. Menstrual cycling optional. Every subsystem independently configurable, like options on a car. <img src="images/scenes/day_1/day_1_9.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> In the other direction, a penis and testicles grown from a client's own tissue, on a body that was born without them. Full size configurable length, girth, proportion. Fully erectile, fully sensate, the nerve mapping calibrated to produce authentic male sexual response from arousal through climax. Testicles that produce testosterone naturally, that manufacture viable sperm if the client desires, that hang in a scrotum grown from labial tissue repurposed so seamlessly that a urologist examining it would find nothing to flag. The prostate, the vas deferens, the complete plumbing of a male reproductive system, assembled inside a body that was born female, indistinguishable from natal anatomy by any test, any scan, any lover's touch. Both directions are fully reversible. A client could transition from male to female, live in that body for years, and transition back or to something else entirely. Dual configurations are available, both sets of genitalia, simultaneously, fully functional, the body's endocrine system balanced by RegenaForm's proprietary hormonal calibration to support both without conflict. Switchable configurations exist at the experimental tier anatomy that shifts between states on command, one set active while the other lies dormant in compressed biological storage, toggled by a neural signal the client learns to control like flexing a muscle. The technology doesn't care about direction. It doesn't care about origin or destination. It sees the body as raw material infinitely plastic, infinitely configurable and the client's desire as the only blueprint that matters. Grow it, shrink it, reshape it, reverse it, start over, try something new. The flesh is clay. RegenaForm provides the kiln. <img src="images/scenes/day_1/day_1_10.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> No surgeon's hands. No operating theatre. No months of recovery, no dilations, no compromises. Just a reclining chair, a cool gel, a warmth that spreads, and a body that wakes up different. Complete. Unmarked. As though it had always been this way. RegenaForm doesn't limit itself to what biology intended. It offers what biology could have intended, if biology had a bigger imagination and a smaller sense of propriety. The technology is miraculous. The ethics are a void. RegenaForm doesn't ask why. They don't require therapy letters or diagnostic criteria or the careful gatekeeping that traditional medicine employs. They offer a menu, a price list, and a smile. The client chooses. The client pays. The body changes. What happens to the person inside it the identity, the psychology, the sense of self that was built on the assumption that the body would stay the same is not RegenaForm's department. <img src="images/scenes/day_1/day_1_11.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> Their clinics have spread through every major city, quiet storefronts in unremarkable buildings, identified only by the chrome helix on frosted glass. The waiting lists are long. The prices are high but not prohibitive calibrated precisely to be just affordable for a person who's desperate enough, just within reach of a person who can see the math working out if they earn enough, stream enough, transform enough, earn more, transform more. The loop is the product. The escalation is the business model. The first procedure is free. [[Eli's Story|start_3]] | <<link "Skip Introduction">><<set $hint to "Find your Apartment and Bed">><<goto neighbourhood>><</link>>Into this world this post-automation, algorithm-governed, attention-commodified, genetically-hackable world step Eli Vance. Twenty-two years old. Five-foot-nine. A hundred and forty pounds of skinny-fat neglect distributed across a frame that nature assembled with the enthusiasm of a substitute teacher filling in on a Friday. He has the kind of face that exists in the space between faces not ugly enough to be memorable, not handsome enough to be noticed, just there, occupying a position in the visible spectrum that the human eye slides past the way it slides past wallpaper. Brown hair, usually greasy. Brown eyes, usually tired. Skin that can't decide if it's pale or sallow and has settled on both. Acne along the jawline that he's had since fifteen and will have until something changes. <img src="images/locations/eli_apartment.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> He tried the normal path. One semester of college computer science, the degree everyone said was "AI-proof," which turned out to be a joke that stopped being funny when the AI learned to code better than the professors teaching it. The financial aid fell through. The motivation followed. He applied for jobs retail, food service, warehouse, delivery and watched each one evaporate between the application and the interview, replaced by a kiosk or a bot or an app or a "restructuring" that was a euphemism for "we bought software." For six months he did gig work food delivery on an e-bike in weather that tried to kill him, for an app that took 40% and offered no benefits and deactivated his account for a week when his rating dropped below 4.7 because a customer lied about a missing order. Then he saw a YouTube video. A guy, roughly his age, roughly his situation, sitting in a room not unlike his, streaming a game to forty viewers and talking about how he made $600 last month. Six hundred dollars. For playing video games and talking. The number lodged in Eli's brain the way a bullet lodges in a wall embedded, permanent, impossible to remove without pulling the whole structure apart. He started streaming the next week. That was eight months ago. He lives alone in a 280-square-foot studio apartment that costs $875 a month, which is $875 more than it's worth. The apartment contains, a mattress on the floor (found curbside, stain of unknown origin), a desk (also found curbside, one leg requires a cardboard shim), two monitors (one refurbished, one dying), a microphone (budget), a webcam (antique), a mini-fridge (humming), a hot plate, a microwave with a broken turntable, and a crack in the ceiling that grows a little every day, splitting the plaster from the kitchenette to his pillow like a fault line in cheap geology. His channel, EliPlays, has 54 followers most of whom followed during a brief raid six months ago and have never returned. His average viewership is between 8 and 15 people, a number that includes bots, accidental tab-leavers, and one dedicated troll named xX_DarkSlayer_Xx who appears daily, without fail, to inform Eli that he is terrible. His lifetime earnings from streaming total approximately $170. His most recent monthly income was $24.50. He plays Gunmetal Requiem, the biggest competitive shooter on Twitch, at the Silver rank the vast, unmarketable middle of the skill spectrum where nobody watches because there's nothing to see. /* <img src="images/scenes/day_1/day_1_13.jpeg" alt="Eli's face after eyelash enhancement" class="scene-image"> */ He eats microwave burritos. He drinks Monster Energy. He sleeps at irregular hours on grey sheets that were once white. He picks at the skin around his thumbnails when he's anxious, which is always. He avoids mirrors. Not out of dysphoria out of disappointment. His social circle is small enough to list in a sentence, Marcus "Marc" Delano, his best friend since middle school, who works part-time at a phone repair shop and doesn't understand streaming and doesn't need to because he shows up with cheese puffs and sarcasm and the specific loyalty of a person who decided a long time ago that you were worth keeping and Kira Nomura, a mid-tier streamer he met in a Discord server, who averages 800–1,200 viewers and earns more in a single session than Eli earns in a quarter, and who talks to him every day with a warmth he can't explain and won't examine because examining it would require asking why a successful, beautiful, razor-sharp 21-year-old woman chooses to spend her time on a guy who peaked at six viewers. Eli has $47 in his checking account. He has no savings. No safety net. His mother works two jobs in another state and communicates through bimonthly Venmo deposits and texts that say "hope you're eating ok." No father gone before the memory formed. No degree, no prospects, no plan beyond the next stream, which will be identical to the last stream, which produced nothing. He is not suicidal. He is not in crisis. He is something worse, he is functional. He wakes up. He streams. He eats. He sleeps. He repeats. The machinery of his life operates at minimum capacity, producing just enough motion to qualify as alive, the way a pilot light produces just enough flame to qualify as lit. He is one of millions a face in the browse-page graveyard, a thumbnail nobody clicks, a voice in an empty room, a person the algorithm has decided isn't worth surfacing and the only thing that distinguishes him from the other millions is the specific shape of his desperation. He doesn't know about RegenaForm yet. He doesn't know that a clinic four blocks from his apartment can reshape his face and rebuild his body and rewrite the equation that has defined his life since the day the algorithm decided he wasn't worth looking at. He doesn't know that the technology exists, that the door is there, that the first procedure is free, that the second will cost just enough to require a third, and the third will require a fourth, and the fourth will require everything. But He will. Let's dive into Eli's desperate world. <<set $hint to "Find your Apartment and Bed">> [[Soul of Eli Should Find his body|neighbourhood]]
